patch_description: The prior programs mainly reward individual direct demands and selected two-hop paths. This design instead estimates the load contribution of plausible direct and two-hop routes, then uses sparse positive couplings to discourage choosing links that would jointly concentrate traffic on the same source or destination. A small, demand-weighted set of relay paths supplies alternatives without allowing zero-affinity routes to dominate. The interaction budget is bounded by the number of nodes, preserving manageable communities; direct rewards remain the primary signal. All weights are normalized together, and the evaluator continues to supply degree penalties.
